{{Quote|The Xi'Dec's planet, Stic, is a world of constant climatological, geological, and biological change. In order to survive, creatures on Stic must be highly adaptible.|Obo Rin, ''Catalog of Intelligent Life in the Galaxy'', Revised Edition|<ref name="GG42" />}}
'''Stic''' was an [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] located in the [[Xappyh sector/Legends|Xappyh sector]]. It constantly underwent rapid climatic, [[Geology|geological]], and biological changes, and is [[Homeworld/Legends|native]] fauna was forced to be adaptive in order to survive. Stic was home to the [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Xi'Dec/Legends|Xi'Dec]] [[Species/Legends|species]]. The Xi'Dec evolved more than 180 different [[Gender/Legends|sexes]], a phenomenon that, after the planet was discovered by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], attracted curious tourists from throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].

==Description==
{{Quote|Tourists from throughout the galaxy come to Stic, not for the planet (which is currently in an unbearably hot phase of its climatic cycle), but to gawk at the variety of Xi'Dec sexes.|Obo Rin, ''Catalog of Intelligent Life in the Galaxy'', Revised Edition|<ref name="GG42" />}}
Stic was a terrestrial [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="GG42" /> located in the [[Stic system/Legends|Stic system]], a part of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Xappyh sector/Legends|Xappyh sector]].<ref name="EAOC Stic" /> A barren world, from [[Realspace/Legends|space]] it appeared [[Color/Legends|gray]] and pockmarked with craters.<ref name="SWR" /> Stic underwent constant,<ref name="GG42" /> rapid<ref name="SWR" /> [[Geology|geological]] and biological change<ref name="GG42" /> as well as severe<ref name="SWR" /> cyclical climatic changes. The continually changing environment of the planet forced creatures living there to be highly adaptive in order to survive.<ref name="GG42" />

==History==
{{Quote|Xi'Dec society was beginning to experiment with atomic fission and had begun fabricating simple computers when their homeworld was discovered by Republic scouts.|Obo Rin, ''Catalog of Intelligent Life in the Galaxy'', Revised Edition|<ref name="GG42" />}}
At some point during the long and involved evolution of its complex [[Reproduction/Legends|reproductive]] system and methods, the [[Xi'Dec/Legends|Xi'Dec]] [[Species/Legends|species]] of Stic developed [[Sentience/Legends|sentience]] as well as a sophisticated civilization that constructed large [[City/Legends|cities]].<ref name="GG41">''[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races]]''</ref> The Xi'Dec were at one point involved in the conflict on Stic known as the [[K'rom wars]], and at another [[Time/Legends|time]], a series of hurricanes destroyed the majority of artificial structures on the planet.<ref name="GG42" />

When the Xi'Dec society had begun manufacturing simple [[Computer/Legends|computers]] and had begun experimenting with [[nuclear fission]], Stic was discovered by [[Scout/Legends|scouts]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. The [[sentientologist]] [[Randamar Parl]] subsequently established contact with the Xi'Dec, and due to the species' multitude of different [[Gender/Legends|sexes]], he believed he had discovered a world inhabited by many sentient species. The sentientologist [[Obo Rin]] eventually included Stic, which at the time was in an unbearably [[Temperature/Legends|hot]] phase of its climatic cycle, and the Xi'Dec in the ''[[Catalog of Intelligent Life in the Galaxy]]''. In that work, Rin described the sentient species that he considered to be the most important in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] and of the most interest to the Republic's successor, the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="GG42" />

==Inhabitants==
{{Main|Xi'Dec/Legends}}
{{Quote|The Xi'Dec answered this challenge by evolving an incredible number of sexes.|Obo Rin, ''Catalog of Intelligent Life in the Galaxy'', Revised Edition|<ref name="GG42" />}}
[[File:Xidecgg4.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Stic was the homeworld of the Xi'Dec species.]]
Stic was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the sentient, [[Insectoid/Legends|insectoid]] Xi'Dec species. In response to the challenges posed by the planet's environment, the Xi'Dec evolved more than 180 different sexes, with the most common sex, [[Xi'Alpha]], comprising nearly six percent of Stic's population. The species evolved very rapidly in response to environmental changes, and new sexes also evolved to fill specific functional niches in Xi'Dec society. That society was based on [[family unit]] that were always comprised of members of different sexes. The [[Politics/Legends|political]] structure of the Xi'Dec society was prone to rapid change, although in general the most power was wielded by the largest and most diverse family unit.<ref name="GG42" />

Since standardization of form was impossible due to the wide variety of body shapes exhibited by the Xi'Dec sexes, the economical system of their society did not adopt mass production. The most highly advanced Xi'Dec [[Scientist/Legends|scientific]] fields were climatology, geological transformations, and biogenetics, and the corresponding specialists, which became employed by the best [[Galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[University/Legends|universities]], formed the principal export of Stic. Another important industry of Stic was tourism, with visitors from throughout the galaxy traveling to the planet&mdash;not to experience the world itself, but rather to marvel at the variety of the Xi'Dec sexes. The Xi'Dec sometimes mistook offworlders of other species for members of rare Xi'Dec sexes, and consequently it was not uncommon for visitors to Stic to receive hundreds of [[Marriage/Legends|wedding]] proposals from the planet's natives within a few [[Standard hour/Legends|standard hours]] after arriving there. The Xi'Dec themselves rarely traveled to the wider galaxy.<ref name="GG42" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Gg4-1.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Stic was introduced in ''Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races''.]]
Stic was first mentioned in ''[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races]]'', a [[1989]] sourcebook authored by [[Troy Denning]] for use with [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''.<ref name="GG41" /> "[[Twinkle, Twinkle Little Star, How I Wonder Where We Are]]," a [[1990]] [[roleplaying game]] source article published in the [[Voyages SF 13|thirteenth issue]] of the ''[[Voyages SF]]'' magazine, placed the planet in the [[Almakar sector]]. Since that article was released outside of the [[Lucas Licensing]] process, its [[canon]]icity within the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity was never confirmed.<ref name="Twinkle">{{VoyagesCite|13|Twinkle, Twinkle Little Star, How I Wonder Where We Are}}</ref>

The [[1998]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']] instead placed Stic in the Xappyh [[Sector/Legends|sector]] and provided the first visual depiction of the planet, an illustration that was also used for sixteen other worlds.<ref name="SWR" /> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' subsequently placed the Stic [[Star system/Legends|system]], and therefore the planet itself, in grid square Q-3,<ref name="TEA" /> and the [[StarWars.com]] [[Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion|Online Companion]] to the book further overrode the ''Voyages SF'' 13 placement by establishing that all of the [[Star/Legends|star]] systems the article had placed in the Almakar sector, except for the [[Almakar system/Legends|Almakar system]], were instead located in other sectors.<ref name="EAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref>
